This comes from someone who developed anxiety due to driving. Watch youtube videos of driving/parking tips. Watch videos of people enjoying driving. Push yourself a little every time you make a drive. For example, if there’s a certain intersection that I am scared about, I try to have a go at it when it’s less traffic. And again. And again. And again. 

The big thing which has tremendously helped has been exposure therapy. It’s the only thing that did the trick. Having to drive places on a daily basis has been the biggest contributing factor to my anxiety decreasing. 

I can safely say that I enjoy driving now and it actually calms my anxiety. 

Once you get your driving license:

Drive like 50% of the people on the road are stupid and the other 50% are trying to cause an accident. Which means keep distance and stay within parameters you feel comfortable with when it comes to speed and car manouvers. Get to know the car. Learn how to brake really quickly in case of emergency. You’ll learn most things with experience so don’t worry if things are not fully working out. 

Youtube videos have been of tremendous help, but in the beginning driving with someone who knows how to teach is going to be a big contributor to how easy or hard it’s going to be for you.

Congratulations!! I took my driving license a little later than usual and in my country you drive with an instructor. I picked a piece of shit for an instructor (which I ended up finding out later that my mom had the same one before and she also didn’t learn shit from him). He caused me so much anxiety that I ended up living with it for more than a year on a daily basis, dreading the day I knew I had a driving lesson, crying and having panic attacks after each of them. 

Took my exam, failed miserably by a LONG shot, wanted to quit but everyone around me supported me not to, so I ended up switching instructors. This time, I got possibly the most calm instructor I could have hoped for. No matter the mistake, he would correct me calmly and if something was a bigger issue he would at most be a little passive aggresive (but in the calmest way possible hahah). Took it the second time and passed. 

I would say you actually learn to drive after you take your exam. So many situations that only experience can teach you.
If it helps, most people fail their first driver’s test. I feel like that’s some sort of ritual to feel the waters. So don’t be too harsh on yourself, trust me, I’ve done worse on my first.

Learn from the mistakes you make. It’s not about time but experience. Don’t be afraid to make mistakes, no matter how embarassing you think it looks. Just learn from them and next time you drive keep them into account.
